blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Customs and compliance in practice is mostly about avoiding the same small errors that stop shipments every week across the industry. The wrong HS code. A signature in the wrong place. A value declared in one currency but the invoice in another. An address that does not quite match across two documents. None of these are difficult to fix in advance; all of them are expensive to fix after customs has stopped the container.

The good compliance manager builds short, specific checklists for each document and each lane, and reviews them whenever the rules change. When a shipment is stopped, the response is not panic; it is a defined process — one phone call, one escalation, one correction filed, one release request.

Customs is not the enemy. It is a system with its own rules, and companies that respect those rules are released quickly. The ones that do not are the case studies other teams read about.

items.q: According to the text, when are the common errors cheapest to fix?
options: Once the release request is filed
After customs has stopped the container
In advance, before the shipment moves
items.why: "None of these are difficult to fix in advance; all of them are expensive to fix after customs has stopped the container."

items.q: What does the text say a good compliance manager does with checklists?
options: Leaves them to the customs authority
Builds specific ones per document and lane, and reviews them when rules change
Uses one general checklist for all documents
Files them only after a shipment is stopped
items.why: "builds short, specific checklists for each document and each lane, and reviews them whenever the rules change."

items.q: When a shipment is stopped, how should the team respond?
options: With a defined process: call, escalation, correction, release request
By changing the HS code immediately
By waiting for customs to release it
items.why: "the response is not panic; it is a defined process — one phone call, one escalation, one correction filed, one release request."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Small, repeatable errors cause most stopped shipments.
Respecting the rules gets your goods released faster.
Customs is an obstacle designed to work against your company.
items.why: Inferência: o texto afirma "Customs is not the enemy… a system with its own rules", contrariando a ideia de que a alfândega trabalha contra a empresa.

items.q: The last line — "The ones that do not are the case studies other teams read about" — suggests that…
options: companies that ignore the rules become cautionary examples of failure
well-run teams never study other companies
customs publishes an official ranking of importers
case studies are the fastest way to release a container
items.why: Inferência: virar "case study" que os outros leem é ser o exemplo de erro do qual as equipes aprendem — algo a evitar.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte treinando o novo assistente de compliance. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Welcome aboard. On your first morning I always cover the same five errors, because ninety per cent of stopped shipments come from them, and every one can be caught before the container ever leaves.

Error one is the HS code. If it is wrong, the goods can be reclassified by customs and the duty must be recalculated — that alone costs us two days. Error two is the signature: it should be signed in the box marked for the exporter, not the consignee. Error three is currency. Every value must be declared in the same currency as the invoice; when they differ, the file is held.

Here is the rule I want you to remember. When a shipment is stopped, you do not panic and you do not email six people at once. You make one call to the broker, you raise one escalation to me, you file one correction, and you send one release request. That sequence should never change.

Customs is not out to punish us. It is a system with rules. Follow the rules, keep the checklist beside you, and most days you will never hear from them at all.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does Charlotte always cover the same five errors on the first morning?
options: Because ninety per cent of stopped shipments come from them
Because the assistant asked to learn them
Because they are the hardest to explain
items.why: "ninety per cent of stopped shipments come from them, and every one can be caught before the container ever leaves."

items.q: What does Charlotte say happens if the HS code is wrong?
options: Nothing, if the invoice is correct
The goods can be reclassified and the duty must be recalculated
items.why: "the goods can be reclassified by customs and the duty must be recalculated — that alone costs us two days."

items.q: According to Charlotte, in what order should the team respond to a stopped shipment?
options: File a correction first, then panic
One release request, then reclassify the goods
One call to the broker, one escalation, one correction, one release request
items.why: "one call to the broker… one escalation to me… one correction… one release request. That sequence should never change."

items.q: What can we infer from "most days you will never hear from them at all"?
options: The assistant will work alone most days
The broker handles everything without the team
A well-followed process usually keeps shipments moving without incident
items.why: Inferência: seguir as regras e o checklist significa poucos problemas — silêncio da alfândega é sinal de que tudo correu bem.

items.q: How would you best describe Charlotte's attitude toward customs?
options: Calm and rule-oriented, treating it as a system to work with
items.why: Inferência: "Customs is not out to punish us. It is a system with rules" — postura calma e orientada a processo, não de medo.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The container was held because the HS code on the declaration was wrong." An HS code is…
options: the standard classification code used to identify the goods for customs
items.why: HS code = código HS, a classificação padronizada da mercadoria usada pela alfândega.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Every value must be ___ in the same currency as the invoice, or the file is held."
items.why: To declare = declarar; declarar o valor de forma consistente com a fatura.

items.q: "We build a separate checklist for each lane we ship on." In logistics, a lane is…
options: a specific shipping route between two points
items.why: Lane = rota; o trajeto específico de origem a destino.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Once the correction was filed, we sent the ___ so the goods could leave the port."
items.why: Release request = pedido de liberação, o documento que solicita a saída da carga.

items.q: "Don't turn a stopped shipment into a case study for the whole team." Here a case study is…
options: an example others study — usually of what went wrong
items.why: Case study = caso de estudo; virar exemplo (aqui, de erro) que os outros analisam.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em compliance e logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The customs manager still has to sign off on the corrected declaration." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new checklist across every lane next quarter." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "When customs stops a container, don't lose your head — follow the process." To lose your head means to…
items.why: Lose your head = perder a cabeça, entrar em pânico — o oposto do processo definido.

items.q: "The broker promised a fix but never followed through, so the goods stayed at the port." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Please flag up any address that doesn't match across the two documents." To flag up means to…
options: draw attention to it as a problem
items.why: Flag up = sinalizar, chamar atenção para algo que precisa ser tratado.
